hook.line: Someone has knocked a tray of pastries off the counter, and everyone looks at Tomás. English says it with stress: it wasn't ME. Spanish adds a little *si* and the pronoun to do the same job.

examples.en: But it wasn't me, it was him!

examples.es: Tú hazme caso, que yo sé lo que digo.
examples.en: You listen to me, I know what I'm talking about.
But she wasn't the one, it was me!

rule:
To protest that you are innocent, start with *si* and say the pronoun out loud.

*¡Si yo no fui!* is not an "if". Here *si* means "but, come on". The pronoun *yo* is not needed for grammar, which is why it sounds so pointed.

It works for anyone: *¡Si ella no fue!* *¡Si tú me dijiste que sí!*

To take control of a conversation, put *tú* in front of a command: *Tú hazme caso*, you listen to me. Then add *que yo sé lo que digo* to say you know best.

Very casual. Use it with friends and family.
smallPrint: Teachers call this an *si enfático* with an explicit subject pronoun: the pronoun carries emphasis, not information.

options: But she wasn't the one, it was me!
She went and so did I!

readAndPick.es: Tú hazme caso, que yo sé lo que digo.
options: Listen to me, I know what I'm saying.
I'll listen to you, you know what you say.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose the right form and type the whole sentence (But it wasn't me!): ¡Si yo no ___! (fui / soy)
yourTurn.why: It happened already, so the past *fui*.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose the right form and type the whole sentence (But I didn't say anything!): ¡Si ___ no dije nada! (yo / me)
yourTurn.why: The spoken *yo* is what gives the protest its force.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: But I didn't do anything!
yourTurn.why: *Si yo no* plus the past of *hacer*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish (about a woman): But she wasn't the one!
yourTurn.why: The pronoun is now *ella* and the verb is *fue*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish (to a friend): You listen to me.
yourTurn.why: A command to a friend, with *tú* in front to take control.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it a protest: Yo no rompí el vaso.
accept: Si yo no rompí el vaso.
yourTurn.why: Just add *si* at the start with the same *yo*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: But you told me yes!
accept: Si tú me dijiste que sí.
yourTurn.why: *Si tú* points straight at the other person.

pitfalls.why: This is fine but flatter; *si* adds the "come on, really" feeling.
Without *yo* the stress is lost, and the stress is the whole point.
The blame is about something that already happened, so use the past *fui*.

personal: Think of something you were once wrongly blamed for, and protest it with *¡Si yo no…!*
